entities.summary: Mateo de Toro Zambrano y Ureta, 1st Count of La Conquista, was a prominent Spanish military and political figure of Criollo descent born around 1735 in the Spanish colony of Quito, Ecuador. He played a key role in the Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire, leading expeditions to the Amazon and the Guiana Shield. His military victories and diplomatic efforts earned him the respect of his contemporaries and the loyalty of his soldiers. In 1809, he was appointed as the Governor of the Viceroyalty of Peru, a position he held until his death in 1811. He left a lasting legacy in the region, as his military campaigns expanded Spanish control over the Andean region and his diplomatic efforts helped to maintain stability in the region. His life was marked by a series of remarkable events, including the Battle of Ayacucho, which marked the final defeat of the Spanish Royalist forces in South America. He was also a patron of the arts, supporting the work of notable artists and writers of his time. Mateo de Toro Zambrano y Ureta's name became synonymous with bravery, cunning, and military prowess, earning him a place in the annals of South American history. His estate, Toro-Zambrano, remains a testament to his wealth and influence, situated in the heart of the Andean highlands.
